chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Halbi and Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, wine is the head of every sin.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of wine being called the 'head of every sin' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise hadith, narrated from the Sixth and Seventh Imams (Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq), establishes wine as the 'head' (ra's) of sin, a metaphor indicating it is the root cause that unravels other virtues and leads to further transgressions. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as the primary theological justification for the absolute prohibition (nass) of intoxicants, distinguishing it from mere legal categorization. The narration underscores the holistic ethical impact of khamr, affecting both spiritual purity and social conduct.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al Halby and Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim and Humran Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said: ‘
The wine is the starting point of every evil’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Jamilah from al-Halabiy and Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Humran ibn ’A‘yan who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, and abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have made it clear that
wine is the head of all sins.’”
